candidate.title: A finite exact certificate for the universal 0.98 heft barrier
candidate.sector: Computer-assisted mathematics and reusable proof certificates
candidate.thesis: A conventional challenge produced a simpler piecewise-linear certificate; exact audit normalization strengthens it beyond the first polynomial construction. Two exact implementations and a cell-average argument prove a universal bound. No exclusive AI, discovery or commercial advantage is inferred.
candidate.goal: Verify h >= 17902560/18258529 >49/50 for every finite one-dimensional exact residue partition with at least two interval points per class.
candidate.successMetric: Both exact verifiers agree for all lengths2..20; an analytic tail covers all longer classes; cell averages cover every n. Frozen final scope and input controls pass, including refusal of uncertified strictness at the bound. External expert review remains pending.

sources.title: Gerry Myerson: finite residue covers and heft question
sources.excerpt: The author defines distinct-modulus residue classes that partition 1 through n, each containing at least two interval elements, and asks whether any has total reciprocal modulus below 0.98. August 2026 updates address other directions. This paraphrase records the inspected question, not an ownership claim.

sources.title: Incongruent restricted disjoint covering systems
sources.excerpt: Myerson, Poon and Simpson introduced this finite covering-system setting and reported structural and computational results. The inspected primary search extract gives heft bounds in terms of interval length and number of classes; the full CORE PDF was unavailable to this audit.

sources.title: Incongruent Restricted Disjoint Covering Systems
sources.excerpt: The authors define incongruent restricted disjoint covering systems with at least two interval elements per congruence class and describe structural families and finite computations. The study preserves the original partition requirement.

sources.title: Paul Robert Emanuel, Covering systems, 2011 dissertation
sources.excerpt: Appendix C, Theorem C.1, printed page215 gives the strongest inspected prior general bound h>sqrt(8)-2. The thesis defines one-dimensional finite residue partitions; its separate two-dimensional examples do not contradict this theorem. Full copyrighted source copies are excluded from the distributable.

witness.theorem: For every n>=2, every one-dimensional exact partition of{1,...,n} into full restricted residue classes, each hitting at least twice, has h=sum(1/m)>=17902560/18258529>49/50. Distinctness is unnecessary; strictness at this exact final constant is not asserted.

proof_obligations.short_classes: Exact line-arrangement boundary maxima for all lengths2..20; independent polygon-edge clipping and direct interpolation agree.
proof_obligations.interior_maxima: Every arrangement cell has S=A*a*d+B*d^2+C*d; nonzeroA gives an indefinite Hessian, and A=0 lets a maximum move horizontally to a boundary.
proof_obligations.long_classes: Zero-extension quadrature gives integral(W)+TV(Wprime)/(8*20^2)=7905/8<18258529/18240 for every length>=21.
proof_obligations.all_interval_lengths: Exact cell-average dual weights transfer the continuous class inequality to every finite n, with no finite cutoff or asymptotic exception.
proof_obligations.fresh_confirmation: 512 seeded exact phase/cell-integral cases, including256 short and256 tail classes, pass; modified normalization and middle-height controls fail.
proof_obligations.interface: Final corrected wrapper independently recomputes the complete proof, rejects altered/missing proof inputs and unsupported scopes, and refuses strictness at the exact final constant.
